t:
Section 7 (a) of said Act of January 3, 1946, as amended, is hereby amended to read as follows:

“The grades and per annum full-pay ranges for positions provided in subsection (a) of section 4 of this Act shall be as follows:

“medical service

“Chief grade, $10,000 minimum to $11,000 maximum.
“Senior grade, $8,800 minimum to $9,800 maximum.
“Intermediate grade, $7,600 minimum to $8,600 maximum.
“Full grade, $6,400 minimum to $7,400 maximum.
“Associate grade, $5,400 minimum to $6,400 maximum.
“Junior grade, $5,000 minimum to $5,750 maximum.



“dental service

“Chief grade, $10,000 minimum to $11,000 maximum.
“Senior grade, $8,800 minimum to $9,800 maximum.
“Intermediate grade, $7,600 minimum to $8,600 maximum.
“Full grade, $6,400 minimum to $7,400 maximum.
“Associate grade, $5,400 minimum to $6,400 maximum.
“Junior grade, $5,000 minimum to $5,750 maximum.




“nursing service

“Assistant Director, $6,400 minimum to $7,400 maximum.
“Senior grade, $5,400 minimum to $6,400 maximum.
“Full grade, $4,600 minimum to $5,350 maximum.
“Associate grade, $4,000 minimum to $4,800 maximum.
“Junior grade, $3,400 minimum to $4,200 maximum.”

fable.w: This section only sets pay grades and salary ranges for federal medical, dental, and nursing service positions. There is no tempting contrary reading: it contains no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section solely establishes salary ranges for specific federal government positions (medical, dental, and nursing services). It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public comment periods, or interactions with states, tribes, or the general public described in the text.

opus.w: This section only sets grades and pay ranges for federal medical, dental, and nursing positions. No outside party takes part in any federal decision, and no rulemaking authority is granted. Amending a statute is not participation in itself, so the answer is No.
opus.b: This section is a pay table. It sets salary ranges for the medical, dental and nursing grades under the Act of January 3, 1946 (the VA Department of Medicine and Surgery). A reader might lean toward "Yes" because it is a formal amendment to a statute. But nothing in it involves anyone outside the federal government. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking authority, advisory body or right to sue.
